Operations

blocks 6 · 6.1 – 6.6
6Operations maintenance, models, calibration and parameters — operator actions and reference, not part of the overview

6.1Maintenance

take a node out of service gently, admin key required

A maintenance window is routing state, not a second control plane for oMLX: the node accepts no new work, running requests finish, a bound thread falls over to the other node. Only when the card says drained is the machine free for an update — at draining (n) wait, do nothing else. The window lives in the maintenance file (placement.maintenance_file, default ~/.ripple/maintenance.yaml) and survives a restart; with minutes it ends by itself, without it runs until someone ends it. It is set and ended on the node card.

nothing set yet — press "Maintenance" on a node card.

6.2Models

take a model on a node out of routing or hide it, including a rule without a row, admin key required

Two levels, both pure RIPPLE state — nothing is loaded, unloaded or changed on oMLX. disabled: RIPPLE sends no more requests for this model to this node; the model stays in /v1/models as long as another node offers it. hidden: the model disappears from /v1/models once every node hides it — Hermes and opencode lose it from their list, which is why the page asks first. in service takes the state back. It is set in the model table, column node; it lives in the model file (placement.model_policy_file, default ~/.ripple/models.yaml) and survives a restart.

The table comes from /healthz and only knows models a node offers right now. A rule for a model the node no longer offers would have no row there — it would live only in the model file and would take the model out of routing again the moment it is offered. Such rules without a row are therefore listed below with the same in service; they are read when this block is opened, with the admin key.

Rules without a row in the model table are read when Operations is opened.

6.3Calibration

operator action per node, admin key required

Measures how long this node needs to load its own models and stores the rate, so the cold-start estimate comes from the node instead of a constant. The node must hold no active thread: calibration loads models and can evict others.

nothing started yet — press "Calibrate" on a node card.

6.4Replication

copy one model from one node to the other, admin key required

The third and last exception to "this page writes nothing": a model is placed on the target node as files, registered there with reload and given the source's parameters. One model at a time, only on explicit instruction. The target leaves the pool for the duration — reload unloads every model there —, running requests finish, a bound thread falls over to the other node. Before the start this block says what is copied, how large it is and how much space is free; an interrupted copy is resumed, not restarted. Runbook: docs/replication.md.

6.6Restart

end the process and let launchd start it again, admin key required

The one control that ends the process it runs in. The process ends, launchd starts it again about a second later. Requests that are still in flight are cut, thread bindings are lost and rebuilt on the first contact, and this page reconnects by itself — the footer then shows the new build.commit. The operator's own session runs through this service: the request that is streaming at that moment ends with the process. That is why a restart with requests in flight needs a second confirmation. Whether the process may end itself at all is launchd's answer, not the page's (/healthz → restart); without the admin key the control stays off and says why.

1 request(s) in flight on node-a · the process ends 1.0 s after the answer
RIPPLE carries the launchd label `ai.hermes.gateway`, but it inherited it from another job: its parent is not launchd (ppid 1321, not 1), so nothing would start it again after it ended — it refuses to end itself. Start it as the launchd job `ai.ripple` to use this control.

blocks 7 · 7.1 – 7.3

7Nodes

The machines that serve the fleet — add one here, take one out with a drain.

A node is read first and written second: the preview asks the machine through RIPPLE (POST /admin/nodes?dry_run=true), shows what it answered and writes nothing. Only the confirmation changes the fleet, and what it changes lives in the runtime overlay — config.yaml stays the hand-written baseline.

7.1Add by address

One address, one preview, one confirmation.

The address is what you would type in a browser: http://host:port. The scheme may be left out.

Nothing previewed yet.

7.2Find in the network

The sweep of <code>ripple discover --scan</code>, over a CIDR.

Every address in the range is asked for its identity on the port given. A sweep is traffic on the network: it runs only when you press the button, and only with the admin key.

7.3Remove a node

A drain, not a cut: no new work, the running requests finish.

A node declared in config.yaml cannot be removed at runtime — the file is the baseline. Disable it instead.
